Answers to common questions and helpful information
How do NFC tags work with Switchly?

Switchly can write NFC tags that trigger actions instantly:

 • Global actions: enable, disable, toggle, or temporarily disable (e.g., 10 minutes).
 • Profile actions: activate a specific profile and then enable, disable, or toggle.

 If the profile on a tag no longer exists, Switchly shows a toast and does nothing.
 All standard tags are supported; only proprietary formats may not work.
Why did my NFC tag stop working after renaming a profile?

NFC tags store the profile name in plain text.
 If you rename or delete that profile, the tag no longer matches.

 Rewrite the NFC tag with the updated name to fix this.

“Pair tag (UID only)” does not write anything to the NFC tag.
 Instead, Switchly only reads the tag UID (hardware ID) and stores it inside the app.

 If UID pairing is enabled, only that exact tag can be used to toggle or unlock Switchly.
 This is useful for read-only tags or if you don’t want the tag to contain a readable action.
What is the difference between “Temporary disable” and “Emergency unlock”?

Temporary disable pauses blocking for a short time (e.g., 10 minutes) and automatically enables it again. You can use it as often as you want.

 Emergency unlock disables all restrictions for a fixed time (e.g., 15 minutes) and can only be used once per calendar day to prevent overuse.
 Both timers are shown on the main screen.
What does “Require NFC tag to disable” do?

When enabled, Switchly can only be disabled by scanning a valid NFC tag.

 Manual toggle, Quick Tile, and certain controls are locked or show warnings.
 This acts like a physical “key” to turn off your restriction profile.
Why are some settings greyed out or show a toast?

Some settings are disabled depending on Switchly’s state. Examples:

 • If “Require NFC tag to disable” is active, manual disabling options are locked.
 • If Emergency unlock is active, its toggle is disabled until it ends.
 • Developer options appear only after tapping “Version” five times.

 Greyed-out entries still show toasts explaining why they cannot be used.
Emergency unlock disables all blocking for a short time (e.g., 15 minutes).\n It can only be used once per calendar day. After it ends, Switchly automatically resumes blocking.
Profiles contain app selections and blocking rules, e.g., “Work”, “Study”, or “Sleep”.\n You can create, rename, duplicate, or delete profiles.\n The active profile is always shown at the top.
How do I add the Quick Settings tile?
Pull down the status bar, open the Quick Settings editor (pencil / “Edit”), and add “Switchly”.\n\n On some devices the label or state may update with a slight delay.

Switchly uses an Accessibility service to detect when you open a blocked app (window/app changes). It only reacts to those events to enforce your profiles. No keystrokes are recorded, and Switchly does not store your screen contents.
Do I need the overlay permission?

No. Newer versions of Switchly do not require the overlay permission. Blocking is handled via Accessibility and a full-screen blocker screen. If you granted overlay in an older version, you can safely revoke it in system settings.
Why can I still see blocked apps in Recents?

Android shows a thumbnail preview of the last screen in the Recents/Overview view. Apps are not allowed to hide or remove the preview of other apps.
Switchly still blocks the app completely: when you tap the blocked app, Switchly immediately kicks you out again and shows the blocker. Tip: You can clear your Recents to remove the old preview thumbnail.
Does Switchly use a lot of battery?

Switchly is event-based: the Accessibility service reacts when apps change, so there is no constant polling. Battery impact is typically low. If you use Wi-Fi/Bluetooth schedules, Android may show an ongoing notification because those features require foreground services on many devices.
All processing happens locally on your device. No usage data or personal information is sent externally.\n Any future cloud features will be optional and clearly explained.
Can I change the app language?
Yes. Go to Settings → General → Language.\n The app restarts for the change to take effect.
Yes. Choose Light, Dark, or System in Settings → General → Theme.\n Premium unlocks additional colors and a custom color picker.
Why does Switchly behave differently on my device?
Some manufacturers restrict APIs that affect overlays, background services, or Quick Tiles.\n Switchly uses only official APIs — behavior depends on your device/ROM settings.
How does backup work if I reinstall Switchly or change phones?

Switchly stores data locally and can be backed up via your Google account.\n When reinstalling with the same Google account, Android may restore profiles automatically.\n You can disable Google backups if you prefer.
What about usage statistics or analytics?
Some analytics may be part of Premium — optional and privacy-friendly.\n They help understand habits and improve the app.\n No tracking across other apps or services.
How can I contact the developer?

Join the community Discord server for feedback and support:

 https://discord.gg/PC5zn2NeCg

 Or contact the dev directly via email:
 andi@saltyy.at
What exactly does Switchly Premium include?

Switchly Premium adds optional features, but core blocking stays free.

 You get:
 • More accent colors and a custom color picker
 • Custom temporary lock and unlock durations
 • Additional Wifi and Bluetooth Schedules
 • Better Insights and statistics

Schedules let Switchly automatically enable or disable a profile based on time, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth.
 • Time-only: choose days and a time window.
 • Wi-Fi: the schedule becomes active while you are connected to a specific network.
 • Bluetooth: the schedule becomes active while a specific device is connected.

 Schedules are optional and never required to use Switchly.
Why do Wi-Fi schedules need Location permission?

Android treats the Wi-Fi name (SSID) as location-like information.
 On newer versions, apps need the Location permission to read the current SSID.

 Without it, Wi-Fi schedules cannot reliably detect which network you are on and may not trigger.

Each schedule can choose how it affects Switchly:

 • Enable profile: enables Switchly and activates the selected profile while the schedule condition is true.
 • Disable Switchly: turns Switchly off whenever the schedule condition is true, but only if it was previously enabled by a schedule.
 • Enable while active, then disable: enables the profile while the condition is true and turns Switchly off once that schedule stops matching.

 For Wi-Fi schedules, pick "Enable profile" if you only want Switchly to start on certain networks without turning off when you leave them.
Switchly can save actions (e.g., switching profiles or toggling modes) as a QR code. You can share or print it.
How do I create a QR code?
Open the QR screen, choose the action/profile, then tap “Create”. You can save or share the code afterwards.
How do I scan a QR code?
Open the QR scanner in Switchly and point the camera at the code. The action is executed immediately.
This lets you enable blocking for a limited time. When the timer ends, Switchly automatically restores the previous state.
If you set a daily limit, Switchly tracks usage time and blocks the app once the limit is reached.
Where can I set a daily limit?
In the app picker, tap the timer/limit icon next to an app, then choose a preset or “Custom”.
How do I remove a limit?
Set the limit to “No limit”. Then the time cap will no longer be enforced.
Where does usage data come from?
What does “Overall” mean in usage statistics?
Are usage and blocker stats included in backups?
Switchly uses Android’s Usage Access permission to detect the foreground app and estimate usage time.

Overall sums up all saved usage data since you started using Switchly (based on locally stored daily values). If you cleared app data or restored an older backup, Overall reflects the currently stored state.
Yes. Cloud Backup includes your locally stored stats (usage time, blocked time, blocks/attempts, runtime, etc.). Restoring brings those values back.
Yes. You can trigger actions when a specific Bluetooth device connects/disconnects (depending on schedule options).
Why is the Quick Tile missing?
Add it via Android’s Quick Settings edit screen. Some OEMs only show tiles after the app has been opened once.
Can I donate to support Switchly?

Premium is intentionally priced very low. If you still want to support development, you can buy Premium as a “tip” or contact me to make a donation.
 I plan to make Switchly open source once I have a small buffer, so I can continue development without stress and without someone immediately copying it 1:1.
